_comment: WFR-68's companion evidence-binding artifact (WFO-LEDGER-COVERAGE property (ii)): binds a reconciliation-table item to the exact dotted unittest test id that discharges it, read by scripts/workflow_state.py's _reconciliation_evidence_by_item() alongside <work_item_id>-ledger-status.json's own per-entry evidence field. Populated incrementally, WF8c session by session (session_target: 'multiple sessions, deliberately not 1') -- this is the first evidence-backfill increment, covering items with an unambiguous, single-purpose test already naming that item number in its own docstring. Every entry below was independently verified (python3 -m unittest <evidence>) to resolve and pass before being recorded here. Items not yet listed here remain unresolved by _pre_flight_wfo_ledger_coverage until a later session adds their evidence -- expected and correct for a checkpoint whose own session_target is multiple sessions.

New test (no prior coverage existed): after a real /accept-scoped-remediation acceptance, state and registry are both re-read from disk/Git alone (git show HEAD:<path>, no in-memory carryover) and select_next_checkpoint re-selects the same outstanding checkpoint -- no new pointer or marker file exists to read

Same test as item 206 (restates the identical GPT-R40-001 failure scenario as its own end-to-end reproduction) -- the checklist-correction-between-review-and-acceptance flow is refused on the stale confirmation and succeeds only on the corrected one

New test (no prior coverage existed): assert_local_generation_matches still refuses a worktree_root mismatch, and still refuses once a genuine ancestor generation_head (verified via git merge-base --is-ancestor, not a fabricated hash) is left behind by an unrelated later commit -- the local-staleness check's original Milestone-8-incident coverage is unweakened by the reviewed_implementation_head/generation_head split

New test (no prior coverage existed): live HEAD exactly equal to reviewed_implementation_head (bare equality genuinely holds), with zero commits made afterward and so no discoverable Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record commit at all -- the pre-WF8B-003 bare-equality branch is confirmed gone even in the one shape where the old rule would have silently accepted

record_bundle_generation's implementation_revision write is a pure +1 on the prior value, independent of any Git history it is called against, so a genuinely new protected-content round always advances by exactly one, never more, regardless of how many metadata-only commits intervened first; combined with test_content_differs_resolves_ordinary (TestResolveBundleGenerationOutcome), which proves an intervening record-gen commit does not stop a later protected commit from classifying as a new ordinary round in the first place

New test (no prior coverage existed): resolve_bundle_generation_outcome never reads .ai-review/<work_item_id>/current/MANIFEST.md at all (confirmed by reading the function -- it derives its decision from approval_review_content_id and Git trailer discovery alone), so deleting it, replacing it with unparseable garbage, or deleting it again all leave the resolved (same_content, t) outcome byte-for-byte identical

New test (no prior coverage existed): record_bundle_generation is a pure state -> state mutator that never touches its input in place, so an interrupted first call (never persisted or committed) leaves the state a fresh session reads unchanged, and re-attempting the identical call from that same starting state is deterministic -- implementation_revision lands on exactly 1, never doubly advanced by the discarded first attempt
